content: Individuals diagnosed with dyslipidemia or hypertension are strongly advised to undergo regular cardiovascular risk assessments. Statins may be prescribed as part of their treatment regimen; however, it is important to note that these medications can increase the likelihood of developing type 2 diabetes in high-risk individuals. Therefore, careful monitoring is essential to ensure that the therapeutic benefits of statins outweigh their potential adverse effects. If side effects such as significant weight gain or an increased risk of fractures surpass the benefits of statin therapy, discontinuation of the medication is recommended. For the management of hypertension and dyslipidemia, lifestyle modifications are strongly encouraged to improve cardiovascular outcomes. Evidence from the Da Qing study demonstrated that intensive lifestyle interventions over a 30-year follow-up period significantly reduced cardiovascular risks in populations at high risk. In high-risk individuals, particularly those with a body mass index (BMI) of 35 kg/m² or greater, elevated fasting plasma glucose levels, or high hemoglobin A1C levels, intensive preventive strategies may be required to effectively reduce cardiovascular risks.
